_note: DRAFT dialogue for the prologue. Story beats follow the narrative sheet; the wording is a proposal. Every line shows in the dialogue box with a portrait, one speaker at a time. who = speaker id, mood = neutral|happy|scared|scream|cry|brave, portrait_frame = a specific portrait file (the Stranger's morph frames), cut = fraction of the line shown before an interruption. Conversations played with auto=true (cutscenes) move on by themselves; barks are single lines during gameplay that move on by themselves and never stop the player.

arrival_car.text: Daddy, we're here! We're here, we're here!
We're here. Listen to that rain.
Can I give Amelia her present first? Before everybody?
You can. Hood up, and you hold my hand across the lot. It's slippery.

hallway.text: It's just the hallway. Hear that? That's the party.
Daddy! Amelia's present! I left it in the car!
We'll grab it after cake, bug. She won't mind.

party_entry.text: You made it! Hi, Adaline! Look at that dress!
On the mats with everybody. Go on, sweetie.

party_entry_2.text: Of course. Punch is right there by the door. Make yourself at home, Ken.

punch.text: Red punch. Sugar with a little extra sugar.
She's going to be up until midnight.

talk_rachel.text: Cake's at seven. Don't let me forget the candles.

talk_denise.text: Oh, you're Adaline's dad! She's a little firecracker, isn't she?
Awful night to be out. My husband couldn't get through to anybody on the house phone all afternoon.
Probably the storm knocking the lines down. Anyway, no television at a kids' party, right? Just cake and screaming.

talk_stranger.text: Well, hello there! You must be Adaline's father. I'd know that smile anywhere. She's got yours.
Not properly. I'm the deacon over at Kennedy Community Church. Half this town comes through our doors on a Sunday.
Your girl came to our Easter egg hunt with Rachel's family. Found the golden egg and showed it to every soul in the building.
She still keeps it on her dresser.
Ha! Good. Good. You're doing right by her, I can tell. Don't let anybody tell you different.
Go on, now, enjoy yourself. And save me a slice of that cake if the little ones leave any.

talk_stranger_again.text: Bless you. Go on, enjoy the party.

talk_kid.text: We're playing lava! Don't touch the floor!

talk_kidgirl.text: My mom did my pigtails for the party. Do you like them?

talk_parent.text: Rachel really went all out, huh? I think there's more balloons than kids.

talk_mom.text: Is yours the one in yellow? She's been teaching mine how to cartwheel.

talk_dad3.text: Third party this month. I think I've had more cake than my kids.

marcus_wait.text: Grab a drink first, man. Trust me, it's going to be a long one.

smalltalk_marcus.text: Ken, right? Adaline's dad. Marcus. I've got the one in the dinosaur shirt.
Good to meet you. She hasn't stopped talking about this party all week.
Ha. Mine either. Rachel went all out this year. Balloons, the cake, the whole thing.
Hey, you hear anything about the lights out on the highway? My brother-in-law swears half the county lost power.

breach_inspect.text: Hey. Hey, buddy... are you okay?
Is that... is that a person?
Kids, stay back. Stay by the table.

lot_reunion.text: I've got you. I've got you. Are you hurt? Look at me.
The man held my hand. He found me.
Please... please, take me with you. My car, I can't... I can't stay out here with those things.
Please. I'll sit in the back. I won't be any trouble. Please.
Get in. Both of you, in the back. Now.

car_1.text: Daddy, what were those? What happened to everybody?
I don't know, bug. Keep your belt on. Stay down.
Thank you. Thank you, thank you. God bless you.
We'll drive straight to her. Okay? Straight there.

car_hit.text: Hold on! Both of you, hold on!

car_church.text: Is that a burn? Did the fire get you?
It looks like a cross. Does it hurt?
Bug, leave him be. He's had a night.

car_reveal_1.text: Hey... your shoulder. That's smoke. You need a hospital.
You can slow down now, Kenneth.

car_reveal_2.text: I know all of their names.

marcus_again.text: Once the cake hits, it's over for all of us. Sugar crash city.

panic: Where's my son? WHERE'S MY SON?
chase: It's in the hall! It's in the hall!
lot: Get in the car! Get in the car!
